focus: Independent mark-resight abundance surveys and municipal bite/PEP surveillance records for evaluating free-roaming dog catch-neuter interventions against external population and human-health outcomes

propositions.statement: In shelter facilities in the Abruzzo region of Italy, the regional adoption rate rose from 45% in 2023 to 49.6% in 2024, with mortality remaining at 2% and average length of stay falling from 104 to 94 days.
Sheltered dogs aged 1 to 2 years and over 2 years had significantly lower odds of adoption compared to younger animals in Abruzzo facilities.

In Jamshedpur, India, following a CNVR intervention neutering and vaccinating over 20,000 dogs, the proportion of sterilised dogs observed on streets rose, yet overall street counts of dogs increased.
Street counts in Jamshedpur CNVR intervention sites averaged 105 dogs in May 2014 and 144 dogs in December 2018, while sterilisation percentage rose from 27% to 50%.
Over the study duration in Jamshedpur, the probability of observed dogs entering the clinic with mange, transmissible venereal tumours, or pregnancy significantly decreased.
The empirical manifestations of compensatory replacement dynamics (the vacuum effect) in free-roaming dog populations are limited despite being ecologically plausible.
Free-roaming animal removal outcomes vary with spatial scale, continuity, reproduction, abandonment, and human-mediated carrying capacity rather than inevitably triggering rapid replacement.
A policy brief for Morocco was compiled via scoping review of published and grey literature through December 2024 to support humane management of stray dogs addressing rabies and hydatidosis.

unresolved_questions: What proportion of free-roaming dog count increases in CNVR-treated areas is attributable to dog immigration or abandoned owned dogs versus increased visibility and detectability of healthy, sterilised dogs during street transects?
At what specific threshold of sterilisation coverage and spatial boundary containment does a CNVR program overcome compensatory replenishment and achieve an absolute reduction in population size?
Does regional shelter performance (e.g., increasing adoption rates from 45% to 49.6% in Abruzzo) exert any measurable downward pressure on local free-roaming dog densities or abandonment rates?
boundaries: These are new source-backed candidates, not independent replication of the original Sri Lankan intervention.
Gemini 3.8 Flash medium and high use the same model family; review agreement is not an independent model consensus.
WHO-hosted regional scholarly material is not automatically an implemented institutional policy or outcome evaluation.
Off-topic official hits were removed by a scoped lexical safeguard; remaining sources still require semantic appraisal.
No verified geographically matched human rabies/PEP time series was obtained in this round.
Do not infer reduced dog abundance or human morbidity from sterilization/clinic counts.
